description.summary: view and manage the screen-capture executable whitelist

protocol.description:
Lets a privileged client (in practice, this compositor's companion shell) read and edit the in-memory, per-executable screen-capture grant table described in `crate::screencopy`'s module doc - the same table prompts (see `ironland-permission-prompt-v1`) populate.
Deliberately not exposed to ordinary clients, the same way and for the same reason `ironland-permission-prompt-v1` isn't: an arbitrary client should not be able to see, let alone silently grant or revoke, another program's screen-capture access.

interface.name: ironland_capture_permissions_manager_v1

description.summary: manager for the capture grant table

interface.description: Binding this global immediately sends one `entry` event per grant currently on file, in unspecified order, describing the state at bind time. From then on, `entry`/`removed` are sent again whenever the table changes - including changes made by this same client's own `set_grant`/`forget` requests, and changes made by another client's (there is normally only ever one client bound to this global, this compositor's own shell, but nothing enforces that).

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stops this client from receiving further `entry`/`removed` events. Doesn't affect the grant table itself.

request.name: set_grant

description.summary: grant or revoke capture access for an executable

request.description: Sets (adding or overwriting) the decision for `subject`, an executable path exactly as named by a prior `entry` event.

request.name: forget
request.description: Removes any decision on file for `subject`, an executable path exactly as named by a prior `entry` event - the next time it tries to capture, it's prompted again from scratch, the same as if it had never been decided on at all.

event.name: entry

description.summary: a grant was added, changed, or is being reported at bind time

event.description: `subject` is an executable path (see `crate::screencopy:: client_identity` in the compositor for exactly what this looks like and why).

event.name: removed
event.description: Sent after a `forget` request (this client's own, or another client's) actually removed an entry - not sent for a `forget` of a `subject` that had no entry to begin with.
